item.title: Chaudanne
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave

Cave and exploration data

  • Cave rating: Advanced
  • Highest cave rating: Advanced
  • Goes to water: Yes

Diving data

  • Water type: Fresh
  • Tidal: No

References

The Chaudanne spring, or cave, is located in Switzerland, in the “Vaudoise” Alps, near the town of Rossinière. Its survey started in the 1960s. Today, this cave has been explored to the depth of about 160 meters and a mximum penetration of 600 meters. It is the deepest cave in Switzerland. The first push dive was succesfully conducted by Cyrille Brandt in 1988. However, future exploration had to wait for almost 20 years. Michael Walz, with his home-made EDO 04 rebreather, made a push dive to about 160 meters on the 19th of February 2006. The Chaudanne Spring Exploration Group is working on the survey and the exploration of the Chaudanne. The cave entrance is on private property. Please respect that and ask for permission at the hotel Chaudanne! Don’t park in front of the hotel. Use the parking near the train station. The conditions should be well if 3 balls are out of the water at the “Chaundanne o metre”. Reel is needed as the line starts after the first shaft at the bottom at around 12m depth.

Portions from ShowCaves.com The Rinquelle (Rin Spring) is the biggest Karst spring of the karst area Churfirsten-Säntisgebiet. The spring is part of a 600m high drop of the Serenbach (Seren brook). With three subsequent drops the waterfall of the small river is not the highest single waterfall, but still one of the highest waterfalls in Europe. At the foot of the steep cliff the Serenbach forms a gorge, the Serenbachschlucht. Soon after it flows into the Walensee. The Rinquelle is located at the foot of the drop, the lowest segment of the waterfall. 48m high in the vertcal cliff is a cave entrance, where an enormous beam of water leaves the mountain. Locally the biggest spring, the Rinquelle is also one of the biggest karst springs in Switzerland. During snow melt and after high precipitation it produces 10 cubic meters per second. But as typical for karst springs, it depends very much on the weather, and during dry periods, or in winter when all water forms snow, the spring has a very low production. During those times cave divers are able to explore the extensive cave system behind.

item.title: Sorgente Bossi
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave

Additional Notes

Location The outlet of the karst spring is not far from the village of Arogno at the foot of Monte Generoso, right next to the road. Along with “Cà del Feree”, “Bucco della Sovaglia” and “Sorgente del Paolaccio”, it is one of the most important sources of Monte Generosso. This limestone massif, which rises to an altitude of 1701m, is to the north and west of Lake Lugano , bordered on the east by Lago di Como and on the SSW by the Capolago-Chiasso zone, the main massif covers an area of ​​about 50km 2 , the whole area of ​​Monte Generoso includes more than 100km 2
